title: Firebase Firestore Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Firebase Firestore course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What groups the book documents?
questions.explanation: A collection groups documents. Each document has an id and named fields, such as a book title and page count.

questions.question: Why use a demo project and emulator?
options: To practise locally without real cloud data
questions.explanation: An emulator imitates the service on your own computer. A demo project id helps keep practice separate from a real cloud project.

questions.question: Who chooses the id in this setDoc call?
questions.explanation: setDoc writes fields at a document path you choose. Without merge, it replaces the document data at that path.

questions.question: Why call snapshot.exists()?
options: To check that the requested document exists
questions.explanation: getDoc reads a document snapshot. Check exists before reading fields, because the requested document may not be there.

questions.question: What happens if you call addDoc twice?
options: The second call always overwrites the first
questions.explanation: addDoc adds a document to a collection with an automatically made id. The returned reference tells you that new path.

questions.question: What happens to fields omitted from this update?
questions.explanation: updateDoc changes named fields while leaving other fields alone. It expects the target document to already exist.

questions.question: What does this where rule keep?
questions.explanation: A query applies a rule to a collection. getDocs returns snapshots for documents that match that rule.

questions.question: What does limit(2) restrict?
options: The number of fields per document
questions.explanation: orderBy sorts query results by a field. limit caps how many documents are returned.

questions.question: What does the returned stop function do?
questions.explanation: onSnapshot sends the current result and later changes. It returns a cleanup function that stops the listener.

questions.question: When is a transaction more suitable than a simple batch?
options: When two fixed sample records are written
When the write depends on a database value you must read
questions.explanation: A write batch applies several writes together. Either the batch is accepted as a unit or it fails.

questions.question: Do these public demo rules protect private user records?
options: No, they are only for the local public sample
Yes, all records become private automatically
questions.explanation: Security rules decide which client reads and writes are allowed. Even a local exercise should name its intended collection and validate important fields.

questions.question: Why check a record's fields?
options: It creates a second cloud database
Stored or received data may not match the expected shape
questions.explanation: A database record can have a shape your UI does not expect. Check values before using them, even when a type annotation looks reassuring.
